Every returned chart supports the billed level, but note-quality signals raise questions about whether that documentation reflects the visits.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern points toward upcoding: the 99215 excess sits mainly in the 0–1 condition groups. The sampled low-complexity 99215s are routine-sounding diagnoses such as Z09 follow-ups, R21 rash, J06.9 URI and M54.50 back pain (e.g., C0260904, C0261123, C0261150). The documentation, however, does not show unsupported billing: none of the documented 99215s fell below the billed level, and supported examples such as C0260989 (back pain) and C0261036 (abdominal pain) record high MDM. That could fit legitimately complex acute workups, but a zero mismatch rate below the noise seen in honest providers is unusual. Combined with the duplicate-note rate, problem-list flags and data-reviewed claims lacking any lab or test line, it is weak evidence that notes may be templated or inflated rather than proof that the visits were complex. C0260989 is also among the late-note examples. A reviewer should first request the audit trail (not received) to check creation and edit timing and cloning. Next, compare the actual note text of the high-MDM low-complexity 99215s (C0260989, C0261036, C0260889, C0260904, C0260925) for repeated language and for data elements that the claims do not corroborate."}
